newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Shevardnadze says NATO's Solana not anti-Russian.
newsitem.headline: Shevardnadze says NATO's Solana not anti-Russian.

text.p: Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze rejected on Thursday Russian claims that NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana was pursuing an anti-Moscow agenda during a tour of former Soviet republics.

"I met this man (Solana) and spoke with him for quite a long time. I have found nothing anti-Russian. Nothing," Shevardnadze, a former Soviet foreign minister, told reporters at Kiev airport after arriving for a two-day visit to Ukraine.

On Wednesday President Boris Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, accused Solana of having "undeclared, behind-the-scenes" aims in making his tour of Moldova, Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan.
Solana defended his right to visit the countries which, like Russia, all participate in NATO's Partnership for Peace programme aimed at building closer ties between former Cold War foes.
"Now the process of formation of a common European and Euro-Asian situation is going on and we (Georgia) will take part in this," Shevardnadze said.
During his visit to Kiev Shevardnadze is due to meet Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma to discuss political and economic cooperation.

Moscow, which still has military bases in Georgia and Armenia and regards the turbulent Caucasus region as its strategic underbelly, is currently embroiled in a war of words with NATO over the alliance's plans to expand eastwards to take in several ex-communist countries in eastern and central Europe.
